title: Query Dictionary Indexer
real_world_story: A search engine suggestion pipeline maintains an in-memory dictionary of verified search keywords. As new trending terms are discovered, they are added to the dictionary, and incoming search requests are validated against the index to confirm whether a query term exists as a complete search token.
problem_statement:
Design an in-memory query dictionary engine that supports Q sequential operations:
1. 'INSERT <word>': Adds the lowercase string 'word' to the query index.
2. 'SEARCH <word>': Checks whether the exact string 'word' exists in the index. Output 'TRUE' if present, or 'FALSE' otherwise.
task: Process all Q dictionary commands and print the result of each SEARCH command on a separate line.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer Q, the number of operations.
The next Q lines each contain an operation: either 'INSERT <word>' or 'SEARCH <word>', where <word> is a non-empty string of lowercase English letters.
output_format: For each SEARCH command, print 'TRUE' if the word exists in the dictionary, or 'FALSE' if it does not, each on a new line.

examples.input:
6
INSERT code
INSERT coding
SEARCH code
SEARCH cod
SEARCH coding
SEARCH algo
examples.explanation: Searching 'code' returns TRUE (inserted). Searching 'cod' returns FALSE (only a prefix, not marked as complete word). Searching 'coding' returns TRUE. Searching 'algo' returns FALSE (never inserted).

complexity.time: O(L) per operation where L is word length

real_world_takeaway: Trie structures provide string search operations bounded by word length rather than dictionary size, making them resilient to massive index growth.
